errors.description: The hooked tongue at the top of the fly is rendered somewhat larger than the drawn hook — it reads at roughly half the waistband depth in height and rather wider, where the drawing suggests about a third. The shape character (rounded hook, not a point or a square) is correct.
errors.expected: hooked tongue about one third of the waistband depth
errors.actual: hooked tongue about half the waistband depth and proportionally wider
errors.correction: acceptable; the shape is unambiguous and the oversize helps rather than hinders legibility

notes:
ADVERSARIAL READ vs /images/blueprints/remote/0c07e29e9fc5__3402.jpg.

WHAT THE DRAWING SPECIFIES: the trouser front with the fly closed, and a red mark drawn ONLY at the very top of the fly where it meets the waistband — a small curled hook shape, like a claw, that rises onto the waistband and turns back down. The rest of the fly is unmarked.

DISCRIMINATION CHECK AGAINST THE SIBLING. The neighbouring option on the same field, 'Pointed Fly' (3406), was generated in the same run, so I cropped both renders and put them side by side at 3x. This one shows a large ROUNDED lobe curling over the waistband; the sibling shows an angular apex with two straight edges meeting. They are unmistakably different shapes, which is the whole purpose of these two assets.

ATTEMPTED REJECTIONS THAT FAILED:
(1) Square-ended fly top, the default? No — the top is a pronounced curve.
(2) The sibling's sharp point? No — there is no apex anywhere on the tongue; it is a continuous rounded curve.
(3) Fly open, which belongs to the zip-fly blueprint rather than this one? No — the fly is closed and pressed, as drawn.
(4) Annotation traced? No red anywhere; the hook is cloth with edge stitching.
(5) Wrong face or wrong region? Trouser front, waistband and fly, correct.
(6) Belt loops missing or invented? Two belt loops present, matching the drawing.

No critical or major findings.
